title: Government Approval for Industry-changing Mergers and Acquisitions before Announcement
what_it_is: Government Approval for Industry-changing Mergers and Acquisitions before Announcement

sections.label: Singapore voluntary merger notification system
sections.summary: Singapore uses voluntary merger notification, with no mandatory requirement to notify CCCS; parties self-assess and may apply for a formal decision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Singapore adopts a voluntary merger notification system, which is similar to that adopted in the UK, Australia and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Under this regime, there is no mandatory requirement for merger parties to notify their merger situations to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Instead, merger parties conduct a self-assessment and, if they are of the view that their merger may give rise to potential competition concerns, they may apply to CCCS for a formal decision on whether their merger would infringe the Competition Act.

sections.label: CCCS powers over unnotified mergers
sections.summary: CCCS can investigate suspected anti-competitive mergers, issue directions including winding up and financial penalties, and impose interim measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: If merger parties proceed to complete an anti-competitive merger without notifying CCCS and CCCS has reasonable grounds to suspect that a merger has infringed the Competition Act, CCCS is empowered to conduct a full investigation and to issue the necessary directions to remedy any anti-competitive effects, including the winding up of the merger and the imposition of financial penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: CCCS may also impose interim measures to protect public interest, where urgent action is required to prevent market confusion and job disruption, while it completes its investigations.

sections.label: US Hart-Scott-Rodino notification threshold
sections.summary: The US has a Hart-Scott-Rodino pre-merger notification requirement above a threshold of about $76 million, reviewed regularly and inflation-adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The US has the Hart-Scott-Rodino pre-merger notification requirement above the threshold of about $76 million, which is reviewed regularly and inflation-adjusted —

sections.label: Mandatory merger notification jurisdictions
sections.summary: Other jurisdictions have mandatory merger notification, such as the EU, Vietnam, the Philippines and the US, but companies may still merge without notifying.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We have mentioned that Singapore's voluntary notification regime is similar to that in the UK, Australia and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: And, indeed, there are other jurisdictions that have a mandatory merger notification regime, such as the EU, Vietnam, the Philippines and the United States; which include the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act, which the Member has raised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: But even in these jurisdictions where there is mandatory notification, the same situation can arise where companies that are determined to implement an anti-competitive merger still choose to go ahead without notifying the competition authorities.
